message.content:
I’m happy to show you how to add that comment.  
Below is a ready‑to‑run `curl` command that will POST the comment to VirusTotal’s IP‑address endpoint.  
Just copy it into your terminal (or your preferred HTTP client) and hit **Enter**.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "data": {
             "type": "comment",
             "attributes": {
               "text": "Confirmed #malware"
             }
           }
         }'
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-X POST` | Sends a POST request. |
| URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` – the endpoint for adding a comment to the IP `192.168.1.1`. |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Authenticates the request with your API key. |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells VirusTotal that the body is JSON. |
| `-d '{...}'` | The JSON payload. VirusTotal expects the comment wrapped in a top‑level `"data"` object. |

### Quick sanity check

If you want to verify that the comment was added, you can fetch the comments for that IP with:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321"
```

You should see your `"Confirmed #malware"` entry in the response.

> **Note:**  
> * `192.168.1.1` is a private‑network address. VirusTotal may not have any public data for it, so the comment will be stored but you might not see any other information about the IP.  
> * If you run into a “404 Not Found” or “403 Forbidden”, double‑check that your API key is correct and that you’re using the right API version (`v3`).

Let me know if you hit any snags or need help interpreting the response!
